chunks: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) forbade the throwing of poison into the cities of the polytheists.

key_terms.السَّمُّ: Poison — here referring to its use as a weapon of warfare, which was known in pre-Islamic Arabia
key_terms.بِلَادِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ: The cities/lands of the polytheists — referring to enemy territories in the context of early Islamic military campaigns
key_terms.نَهَى: Forbade — an explicit prophetic prohibition (nahy) carrying jurisprudential weight

ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet Muhammad prohibit the use of poison in warfare against enemies?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq from Imam Ali, reports a prohibition issued by the Prophet Muhammad against the use of poison as a weapon in warfare against enemy territories. This reflects an early Islamic principle of limiting harm in warfare and prohibiting indiscriminate or treacherous methods of killing, even against non-Muslim adversaries. The ruling upholds ethical military conduct by forbidding weapons that cause indiscriminate mass casualties.
